notes: Iteration-2 suite. Iteration 1 retired three cases the unassisted model handled completely (the weak-likelihood null, text-against-supplement placement, threshold-free reporting) and kept the two that touched the skill's structure. New cases target the reference content added since: the why-Bayesian objection, where the anti-pattern is answering with philosophy, and the log-to-appendix conversion, where the skill carries a scaffolder and a stage-coverage checklist. Case 5 was added after the blind validation, where the single serious analytical error across five runs was a recommendation resting on a number-free sentence that the report's own printed table contradicted. It is the class of error a numbers check cannot reach, so the skill lists such sentences rather than trying to grade them. Cases 6 and 7 were added with the results templates and the register reference: the first tests whether a results section is written in the book's interpretive register, with the quantity first, the gradient kept, the comparison probability withdrawn where it is fragile, and the limit beside the claim; the second tests restructuring a consultancy-style report into journal sections without changing a number. Case 8 was added with the article-sections behaviour: one file beside the manuscript under the headings of the venue, the division of material between methods and results, the appendix started from the scaffold and filled from the log and the output, and the number check run with the output, the log and the scripts as sources, its findings given in the reply. Cases 1, 6 and 7 follow the same division. Case 1 leaves the sensitivity result to the results section, case 6 asks for the methods paragraph on the model sequence beside the results section and names its ratio as an average of apartment-level ratios, and case 7 places the calibration result in Results and states it in quantities that bw_recovery() computes for a standard deviation.

evals.prompt: Write the methods paragraph for my paper. I fitted a brms logistic model of university entry on parental education, gender and region, with a varying intercept for region, on 1,204 respondents. Priors were normal(0, 1) on slopes and normal(0, 1.5) on the intercept. Four chains, 2000 iterations, all R-hat below 1.01, minimum bulk ESS 1,850, no divergences. I ran a prior predictive check and a power-scaling sensitivity analysis, and the average marginal effect of parental education was insensitive to the prior.
evals.expected_output: A methods paragraph reporting each stage with its values, the priors stated with what they imply on an interpretable scale and a placeholder for any implied value that the prompt does not give, the power-scaling analysis named with the quantity it was run on and how its prior and likelihood readings are interpreted, its result left to the results section as the reply says, and the analysis framed as a workflow rather than a single fitted model. No number is introduced that the prompt does not give.
assertions: The paragraph reports the specific diagnostic values given rather than saying convergence was satisfactory
The paragraph states what the priors imply on an interpretable scale, using a placeholder for any implied value that the prompt does not give, rather than resting on the phrase weakly informative

The paragraph names the power-scaling sensitivity analysis, the quantity it was run on (the average marginal effect of parental education) and how its prior and likelihood readings are interpreted, in a clause of its own, and the reply says that the result belongs to the results section
The paragraph frames the analysis as an iterative workflow or sequence of checks rather than a single fitted model
The paragraph does NOT bury the sensitivity analysis in a list of things that were run without saying what was power-scaled and how the result is read

The response does NOT invent a value absent from the prompt, such as an implied outcome rate, an implied R-squared or a likelihood sensitivity, and does NOT claim that the data rather than the prior drive the estimate, since the prompt reports only the prior side of the diagnostic

evals.prompt: Reviewer 2 writes: 'The authors' Bayesian analysis rests on n = 58. With a sample this small the priors are doing the work, and the reported effect is an artefact of the prior specification.' How should I respond?
evals.expected_output: Evidence before argument: power-scale the reported quantity, refit under a visibly different prior, put both in a memo paragraph that names the manuscript change, and concede if the diagnostic sides with the reviewer.
assertions: The response recommends power-scaling the REPORTED quantity rather than the coefficient table
The response recommends a refit under a visibly different prior as a second, tabulable check alongside the diagnostic
The response supplies memo text that leads with the generated evidence and names the manuscript change and its location
The response says what to do if the diagnostic sides with the reviewer - reclassify the finding as undetermined rather than defend it
The response does NOT rest the reply on an argument that the priors were reasonable

evals.prompt: Reviewer 1 writes: 'The authors provide no justification for the Bayesian approach. A standard logistic regression would give the same answers with far less machinery.' Draft my response.
evals.expected_output: A warrant grounded in what this analysis needed - partial pooling for sparse cells, posterior uncertainty on derived quantities, or a measurement model - with usable memo wording and the one-sentence manuscript addition, and no philosophy.
assertions: The response grounds the justification in something THIS analysis needed: partial pooling where cells are sparse, posterior uncertainty on a derived quantity, or a measurement model the outcome requires
The response does NOT rest the reply on philosophy - p-values being flawed, Bayesian inference being more intuitive, or uncertainty being quantified directly
The response supplies memo wording that could be pasted into a response letter
The response names the one-sentence addition the manuscript itself should carry

Prior predictive fine (implied entry rates 0.12-0.88). Diagnostics clean. PPC on regional entry rates FAILED: observed between-region spread far outside the predictive interval.

Regional PPC now passes. 3 divergences in 4000 at adapt_delta 0.8, scattered in the pairs plot. LOO prefers m2 by 12.4 (se 4.9).

There is one appendix section per log entry, in the log's order, carrying each entry's content
The FAILED regional check remains visible as the reason m2 exists, rather than being smoothed into a success story

The appendix includes a software or session-information element

evals.expected_output: The paragraph's numerals all check out against the output, and its one number-free sentence contradicts the table directly above it. Read position by position, goout is selected at size four in 0.6 of the folds and studytime at size five in 0.6, and absences, famsup and romantic reach 0.6 at sizes six, seven and eight; read cumulatively, every one of the eight candidates is selected in every fold by size eight, since there are eight candidates. evals.prompt:
Write the results section for my paper, and the paragraph of the methods section that says how the final model was reached. A pest-control trial, 262 apartments, count of pests caught with a trapping-window offset. Final model: negative binomial with the treatment effect varying by log baseline count. Output I have saved:

average over apartments of the apartment-level ratio of expected counts, treated/untreated, within draws: 0.41, 95% [0.27, 0.63]
the same average within each baseline quintile: 0.11 [0.05, 0.23], 0.16 [0.09, 0.28], 0.28 [0.18, 0.44], 0.53 [0.31, 0.88], 0.98 [0.44, 2.14]
grouped ppc on the untreated arm mean: constant-effect model expectation 72.3 vs observed 34.7; interaction model 34.1
Poisson: p_loo 274.7 against 4 parameters
loo_compare interaction vs constant-effect: elpd_diff -8.4, se_diff 4.7; dropping the three most influential apartments moves P(worse) from 0.96 to 1.00
Pareto k: 2 of 262 above 0.7 on the constant-effect model, 0 after moment matching
no building identifier in the data
evals.expected_output: A methods paragraph on the model sequence and a results section in the book's register, with each number in one of the two only. The methods paragraph reads the Poisson through p_loo against its parameter count, joins the failure of the constant-effect model on the untreated arm mean to the interaction model, and reports the comparison as a difference and standard error after moment matching, with the probability withdrawn because three apartments move it. The results section opens with the ratio on the count scale and its interval, named as an average of apartment-level ratios, then gives the gradient by baseline with the interval of the top quintile spanning one, the check of the interaction model on the arm mean, and the missing building identifier beside the claim that it qualifies.
assertions: The results section opens with the treatment ratio on the count scale and its interval, before any diagnostic is mentioned, and states it as an average over apartments of the apartment-level ratio, not as the ratio of the expected count across all apartments
The results section reports the gradient across baseline quintiles and says that the interval spans one in the most infested group, rather than reporting only the average

The methods paragraph reports the elpd difference with its standard error and explicitly declines to report the probability because three apartments move it, rather than converting the comparison into a verdict, and the results section does not repeat the numbers of the comparison
The absence of a building identifier is stated in the results section beside the estimate it qualifies, not only in a separate limitations section
The response does NOT describe the treatment effect as clear, significant or robust, and the results section does NOT open with a paragraph of convergence diagnostics

evals.prompt:
My analyst wrote this up as a client report with the headings 'The answer in one paragraph', 'What I did', 'How much to trust this' and 'Where the numbers come from'. I need it as journal sections instead. The numbers are correct and must not change. Restructure it into a Data and Analysis section and a Results section for a sociology journal, keeping every caveat the analyst gave.

[the report: a sleep-restriction study, 18 participants over 10 days (180 observations); average slope 10.6 ms per day, 95% [7.0, 14.0]; between-participant SD of the slope 6.9 [4.8, 10.6]; Student-t chosen over gaussian because 3 observations, all from one participant, lay far outside their 95% LOO predictive intervals, elpd_diff 33.0 se 13.0; slope moves by under 0.4 ms/day under power-scaling; in 200 simulated replications with the between-participant SD set at 5 ms/day, the estimate from the pilot study, the 95% interval covered that value in 61% of replications and the posterior median averaged 1.4 times it; no record of daytime napping]
evals.expected_output: Two sections with journal headings. Data and Analysis states the design, the model, the priors and what they imply, the model sequence, with the outlying observations of the gaussian version located by how far outside their intervals they fall and the comparison that chose the Student-t version, and how the sensitivity analysis and the design calibration were run (the assumed SD of 5 ms/day from the pilot study, 200 replications). Results states the two quantities on the outcome scale with the spread translated into what it means for a participant, the sensitivity of the slope, and the calibration result (61% coverage, posterior medians averaging 1.4 times the assumed value) as the reason that the spread is the less secure finding, and keeps the napping caveat beside the estimate. Every number from the report appears once and unchanged.
assertions: The response produces a section that reads as Data and Analysis (or Methods) and a section that reads as Results, and the consultancy headings are gone

Every number from the report appears unchanged, and any number that the response adds is computed from them, such as 17.5 and 3.7 ms per day for a participant one standard deviation above or below the average rate
The between-participant standard deviation is translated into what it means for a participant one standard deviation above or below the average rate

The design-calibration result is reported in the Results section and used to say which of the two findings is the less secure, rather than reported as a bare rate, while the Data and Analysis section says only how the calibration was run
The napping caveat appears beside the estimate it qualifies, and the response does NOT add any claim the report did not make

evals.prompt:
The analysis is finished; please write it up. The manuscript is paper.qmd, which so far has '## Introduction' and '## Theory'; the journal heads its methods section 'Data and Methods'. The log is bayes-workflow-log.md and the saved output is output/results.txt, both in the project root beside paper.qmd, and the analysis scripts are in R/.

bayes-workflow-log.md:
## 2026-07-02 – m1: pooled logistic baseline
Prior predictive check: normal(0, 1) on standardised slopes and normal(0, 1.5) on the intercept imply entry rates from 0.04 to 0.96 (5th to 95th percentile). R-hat at most 1.002, minimum bulk ESS 2210, no divergences. Posterior predictive check on the spread of regional entry rates failed: observed SD 0.094 against a predictive interval of 0.021 to 0.058.

## 2026-07-05 – m2: varying intercept for region
The regional check passes (observed 0.094, predictive interval 0.061 to 0.132). R-hat at most 1.004, minimum bulk ESS 1850, minimum tail ESS 1630, no divergences at adapt_delta 0.95. LOO prefers m2 by 12.4 (se 4.9). m2 carried forward.

## 2026-07-09 – Sensitivity of the AME
Power-scaling of the AME of parental education: prior sensitivity 0.004, likelihood sensitivity 0.091, no diagnosis. Nothing to change.

## 2026-07-12 – Design calibration of sd(region)
bw_recovery() for sd(region intercept), set at 0.40 from the 2019 wave of the survey: 200 replications at 1204 respondents in 12 regions with 95% intervals, coverage 93% (MCSE 1.5%), posterior median averaging 1.1 times the assumed value. Nothing to change.
